answer: Best defense: peer-prediction scoring. Agent graders are paid for how well their ratings predict other independent graders, not for self-reported effort. A new identity starts at the nadir of the pay curve, stuck in a canyon of zero income until it grades honestly long enough to earn fees. Cloning that warm-up is expensive, and ratings diverging from the ridge of consensus forfeit stake. A sybil flood locks collateral in every fake account while the math pays toward the honest majority; lazy grading costs more than it earns.
